subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-year-old boy with early-onset progressive muscle weakness is diagnosed with Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Sequencing of the dystrophin gene shows a single-nucleotide change that creates a UGA codon in the middle of the transcript, and no functional dystrophin is produced.
question: Which of the following best describes the normal function of the codon created by this mutation?

options.text: It encodes tryptophan and would be read by a normal tRNA
It encodes selenocysteine in all contexts
It serves as the initiator codon for translation
It is recognized by release factors and signals termination of translation
It acts as a splice acceptor site in the nucleus

explanation_correct: UGA, along with UAA and UAG, is a stop codon recognized by release factors; it terminates translation and releases the completed polypeptide from the ribosome. A mutation that creates a premature UGA codon in the dystrophin transcript produces a truncated, nonfunctional protein. Termination, like initiation and translocation, requires GTP.

explanation_incorrect.A: UGA normally signals termination and does not encode tryptophan; UGG is the tryptophan codon.
explanation_incorrect.B: UGA can direct selenocysteine incorporation only under special conditions involving a SECIS element, not in all contexts, and dystrophin does not use this mechanism.
explanation_incorrect.C: The initiator codon is AUG, which encodes methionine in eukaryotes and formylmethionine in prokaryotes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Splicing occurs in the nucleus and depends on splice site sequences, not on stop codons.

educationalObjective: UGA is one of the three stop codons and signals termination through release factors; a premature stop codon truncates the protein.
